This bill would stop the Commonwealth and its associated bodies from giving financial help to coal-fired power plants.
It would ban direct payments, loans, underwriting, government bonds, contracts for difference, floor price guarantees, equity, capacity payments, and indemnity from carbon risk.
Exemptions would allow the Commonwealth to carry out normal regulatory processes, support affected workers and communities, fund research, or manage power station closures.
Prohibits the Commonwealth from providing financial assistance for building, refurbishing, or purchasing coal-fired power stations.
Bans indirect assistance such as underwriting or guaranteeing someone else's financial obligations.
Lists specific prohibited forms of assistance including direct payments, loans, and equity.
The Commonwealth, associated Commonwealth bodies, and the Australian taxpayer.

The Coal-Fired Power Funding Prohibition Bill 2018 was introduced to prohibit the Commonwealth from providing financial assistance for building, extending, or purchasing coal-fired power stations, aiming to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and protect taxpayers from financial risks associated with stranded assets and carbon liability underwriting. The bill includes exemptions for regulatory functions, worker and community transition support, general research, and managed closures.
